summary: Step 5 + the F1/F2/F3 hardening slice are correctly and completely implemented across backend and frontend, with no blocking findings. /exam-sessions CRUD applies the Nhom-3 defaults (3/2/120/0), enforces inclusive config ranges and VI/EN language with VALIDATION_ERROR, starts DRAFT, and is subject-scope guarded on every route (requireAuth + requireRole('LECTURER')). The pasted student-code roster is all-or-nothing (unknown or non-STUDENT codes return {ok:false,errors:[{code,error}]} with zero writes, surfaced as HTTP 422); examiner assignment rejects non-LECTURER ids. The DRAFT->OPEN->CLOSED state machine throws 409 INVALID_TRANSITION on illegal moves, gates open on >= main_question_count APPROVED topic questions (409 NOT_ENOUGH_QUESTIONS otherwise), locks the used rubric(s) via the newly-added rubricRepository.setLocked inside a transaction (wiring the previously-unreachable Step-3 lock), and pre-generates main-question audio through a MOCK TTS seam only. The mock TTS adapter is a pure crypto-hash with no network/IO and the 'google' branch throws NOT_IMPLEMENTED without calling out, so no real Google TTS/Bedrock/STT call is introduced. pickMainQuestions does a Fisher-Yates random pick of APPROVED ids and is exported for Steps 6-7. F1 adds lecturer->subject scope to BOTH questionService and rubricService with ADMIN bypass, null-subject lenient fallback, and lazy subject-set loading so the mock DB path is unaffected. F2 mounts /topics, /evaluations, and /api/lecturer behind requireAuth without deleting the routers. F3's resolveJwtSecret hard-fails a blank JWT_SECRET when awsMockMode===false and keeps the dev/mock/test fallback. Migration 014 is additive/idempotent (three CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS) and no applied migration 001-013 was edited. Verification: backend unit 206 pass (baseline 163 not weakened), backend e2e 86 pass / 21 skipped / 0 fail offline (baseline 81 preserved; DB-gated exam-session flow self-skips without TEST_DATABASE_URL as designed), frontend vite build compiles clean, and oxlint reports 0 errors (only the pre-existing set-state-in-effect warning pattern).
